# 佛說五大施經

**ID:** T0706
**Volume:** T16
**Category:** 經集部類
**Original Category:** 經集部
**Byline:** 宋 施護等譯
**Dynasty:** 宋
**Date:** 980
**Juans:** 1
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T0706

## Contributors
- 施護 (A000844)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

T706 in one fascicle is a Northern-Sòng translation by [Dānapāla](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%BD%E8%AD%B7) (lifedates uncertain, fl. 980–1017) of a brief Mahāyāna sūtra on the *pañca mahādāna* — the "five great gifts" — i.e. the five fundamental moral abstentions (the five precepts) recast as positive *dāna* (gifts) of safety from oneself to all sentient beings. The Taishō witness opens "西天譯經三藏朝奉大夫試光祿卿傳法大師賜紫沙門臣施護等奉詔譯" — giving the standard Sòng-imperial-honorific colophon for [施護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%BD%E8%AD%B7) at the Yìjīngyuàn translation programme.

**Abstract**

The Buddha addresses the *bhikṣu*-saṅgha at Jetavana on the *wǔ zhǒng dàshī* 五種大施 ("five varieties of great gift"). The sūtra's doctrinal innovation is to reframe the standard five *śīlas* — abstention from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and intoxicants — as positive gifts: by abstaining from killing, the practitioner gives all beings the gift of *abhaya-dāna* 無畏施 (gift of fearlessness, freedom from harm); by abstaining from stealing, one gives all beings the gift of safety in their possessions; etc. The five *śīlas* are thus reconceived not as restrictive prohibitions but as positive bodhisattva *dānas*, integrated with the *pāramitā* framework. The work is short and aphoristically structured.

[施護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%BD%E8%AD%B7) / Dānapāla was one of the principal translators at the late-tenth-century Translation Institute, working alongside [天息災](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%A9%E6%81%AF%E7%81%BD) and [法天](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E5%A4%A9) under Sòng imperial patronage. Composition window: [施護](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%96%BD%E8%AD%B7)'s active translation period at Kāifēng, 982–1017.
